input.summary: Jess O'Riley says her designs often return to festivals in a completely different form

title: Relief as Eccles, Trafford Centre and Altrincham tram lines open

input.lead: Altrincham, Eccles and Trafford Centre lines reopen after a £150m track upgrade in Greater Manchester
input.summary: Altrincham, Eccles and Trafford Centre lines reopen after a £150m track upgrade in Greater Manchester
input.evidence_text: Three weeks of disruption to commuters in Greater Manchester has come to an end after the one of the biggest ever upgrades to the region's tram network The Eccles, Trafford Centre and Altrincham lines on the Bee Network reopened earlier, with services to Manchester Airport and East Didsbury reconnected to the wider network They were closed on 13 July as part of a £150m upgrade to 6km of track between Trafford Bar, Cornbrook and Deansgate-Castlefield It comes after passengers had been forced to take busy replacement buses and trains for weeks while the work took place A section of the track by Trafford Bar was 30 years old and was torn out and replaced as part of the work Transport bosses say the repairs mean the tracks will not need replacing for another 30 years and passengers should see direct benefits once the lines reopen

title: Barack Obama and other US presidents with links to the North West

input.lead: Which former US presidents have family links to the north-west of England?
input.summary: Which former US presidents have family links to the north-west of England?
input.evidence_text: Barack Obama and other US presidents with links to the North West - BBC News Image source, Bill Streicher / USA TODAY Image caption, The north-west of England plays a part in the family histories of both Barack Obama and George W Bush By Marc Waddington North West Published 2 August 2026 Former US President Barack Obama is coming to Manchester later this year as his stage show returns to the UK. His visit has renewed hopes that he might make the short journey down the M62 to Liverpool – a city that played a significant role in his family's history. But Obama – whose great-great-grandfather sailed to America from the port city in 1850 in search of a better life – is not the only former US president with ties to the north-west of England. The links between some of his predecessors and the region are even stronger. Visitors to Manchester can find a statue of Abraham Lincoln. During the American Civil War, Manchester boycotted cotton picked in the southern states in protest against the use of slave labour by the Confederacy. This led to mass unemployment and poverty among textile workers in Manchester. Lincoln wrote a letter praising the working people of the city for their "sublime Christian heroism" in helping the Union to prevail. The statue, by George Grey Barnard, was originally erected in the grounds of Platt Hall in Platt Fields Park in 1919. It was moved to Lincoln Square on Brazennose Street in 1986, where it has remained ever since. Image source, Reuters Image caption, Liverpool is part of Barack Obama's family history Both Presidents Bush can trace their families back to Chorley, in Lancashire, while the story of George Washington – the very first of the First Citizens – began in the village of Warton on the outskirts of Lancaster. input.evidence_text: By Sir John Curtice Professor of politics at the University of Strathclyde The consistent message of the opinion polls since the new prime minister walked into Downing Street almost a fortnight ago is that Labour is enjoying a "Burnham bounce". And this has now been confirmed by Polls conducted in the last week put Labour on average in the mid 20s. It is the party's highest standing since the beginning of last year and compares to their rating of 19% in late June when Sir Keir Starmer announced he was standing down But with Reform polling only narrowly behind Labour, Burnham's party still has a long way to go before it can face the prospect of fighting a general election with confidence All but one of the recent mid-term changes of prime minister have been followed by an increase in the popularity of the incumbent government. Support for Labour rose by seven points after Gordon Brown replaced Tony Blair in 2007, while the Conservatives enjoyed a six-point bounce We should also bear in mind the depth of the electoral hole that Burnham has inherited as Labour leader. input.evidence_text: Real Life 'Sight loss won't stop me climbing a 4,221m mountain in the Swiss Alps' Lucy Hobson could become the first woman with sight loss to reach its summit News Rachael Davis, PA and Stephen Topping Senior reporter 06:05, 03 Aug 2026 Updated 06:41, A Stockport mountaineer could become the first woman with sight loss to reach the summit of a huge Swiss Alps mountain. Lucy Hobson, 33, will tackle Zinalrothorn later this month The 4,221-metre peak was first climbed in 1864, but Lucy is looking to make history when she tackles the mountain. Lucy has optic atrophy, a genetic condition where the optic nerves shrivel rather than form, which causes permanent vision loss While her condition has worsened over the years, Lucy refuses to let it stand in her way. "When I started doing these kinds of challenges, it was just for myself, really," she said "It is what I enjoyed, and it is what made me happy. I always suffered a lot with depression, and this helps me a lot "And then, aiming a bit higher... (I can) show people that if I can do it, if you're thinking about wanting to do something and there's something stopping you, just go and do it. Because once you take that first step, you'll never look back."

Lucy Hobson, 33, will tackle Zinalrothorn later this month The 4,221-metre peak was first climbed in 1864, but Lucy is looking to make history when she tackles the mountain. Lucy has optic atrophy, a genetic condition where the optic nerves shrivel rather than form, which causes permanent vision loss While her condition has worsened over the years, Lucy refuses to let it stand in her way. "When I started doing these kinds of challenges, it was just for myself, really," she said "It is what I enjoyed, and it is what made me happy. I always suffered a lot with depression, and this helps me a lot "And then, aiming a bit higher... Lucy has optic atrophy, a genetic condition where the optic nerves shrivel rather than form, which causes permanent vision loss While her condition has worsened over the years, Lucy refuses to let it stand in her way. "When I started doing these kinds of challenges, it was just for myself, really," she said "It is what I enjoyed, and it is what made me happy. input.evidence_text: Greater Manchester Police were called to Duchy Road, Salford, on Friday 24 July by the family of 28-year-old Ricky Swindells, who said he was experiencing a mental health crisis The Independent Office for Police Conduct (IOPC) said it would be investigating the "decision-making" of the officers and the "necessity, proportionality and rationale" for handcuffing Swindells GMP said it had referred itself to the IOPC and was supporting the investigation, and that its officers had acted to try and "de-escalate" the situation The initial results of a post-mortem could not determine the cause of Swindells' death and further forensic work, including toxicology testing, is ongoing The IOPC said it had reviewed body-worn camera footage from the officers involved, which showed them stating he was being restrained "for his own safety" The watchdog said Swindells' family were on the phone to the ambulance service at the time police arrived and told the officers he was autistic and in "significant distress"

Positive Steps provides young people with support, careers advice and guidance after school, or between 19 and 25 if they have an Education Healthcare Plan (EHCP), helping them to move into education, training or employment. Only 59 young people out of 7,177 are currently unaccounted for – 0.8 per cent of the borough's young people. A council spokesperson said: "These figures demonstrate the positive impact of the support available to young people across Oldham. A breach of the order will result in arrest.
